summary: Defines two MIB modules for managing label-switching-controlled Frame Relay and ATM interfaces. They build on the interface stacking defined in MPLS-LSR-STD-MIB and MPLS-TE-STD-MIB. It is standards-track.

eli5.summary: A control panel for looking at and adjusting older kinds of network links when they are used with a label-based routing system.

subtitle: Two SNMP MIB modules for managing MPLS interfaces that run over ATM or Frame Relay links.

tldr.problem: MPLS routers can use ATM or Frame Relay links where labels ride in link-layer fields, but the MPLS-LSR-STD-MIB had no way to say which interfaces work that way or how they are configured.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4368 defines MPLS-LC-ATM-STD-MIB and MPLS-LC-FR-STD-MIB. Each adds a table that sparsely extends the MPLS interface table with the VPI/VCI or DLCI settings for label-controlled interfaces.
tldr.outcome: Operators can use SNMP to monitor, and optionally configure, label-controlled ATM and Frame Relay interfaces, with security guidance to protect writable objects.

today: RFC 4368 is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the Two MIBs Are For
sections.content:
RFC 4368 defines two MIB (Management Information Base) modules that describe how label-switching-controlled Frame Relay (RFC 3034) and ATM (RFC 3035) interfaces can be managed. They build on the interface stacking in the MPLS-LSR-STD MIB (RFC 3813) and the MPLS-TE-STD MIB (RFC 3812).

The modules sparsely extend the mplsInterfaceConfTable of the MPLS-LSR-STD MIB, so that a manager can tell which MPLS interfaces have LC-ATM or LC-FR capability.
sections.eli5: Some network links are special and carry labels in an unusual spot. These two lists let a person see which links are special and how they are set up.

sections.title: Label-Controlled Interfaces
sections.content:
On an LC-FR interface, packets carry labels in the DLCI field. An LC-ATM interface is an ATM interface controlled by the label switching control component. A received packet is treated as labeled, and its top label is inferred from the Virtual Channel Identifier (VCI) field, or from the combined Virtual Path Identifier (VPI) and VCI fields.

Two LDP peers connected over an LC-ATM interface use LDP negotiation to decide which case applies, though static label configuration is also possible. When LDP distributes labels for these interfaces, label information may be in the MPLS-LDP-ATM-STD-MIB or the MPLS-LDP-FRAME-RELAY-STD-MIB, both from RFC 3815.
sections.eli5: Normally a package has its address on a sticker. Here the address is written in a different box on the shipping form, depending on the kind of link.

sections.title: Sparse Tables Extending the Interface Tables
sections.content:
LC-ATM interfaces carry labeled MPLS traffic, so they are MPLS subinterfaces with ifType = mpls(166). Because they may carry ATM- or Frame-Relay-encapsulated traffic, it helps to identify them. Each module is a table whose entries line up with entries in the interfaces table (RFC 2863) and the mplsInterfaceTable.

The RFC's example has five interfaces. Those at ifIndex .2 and .4 are of type mpls, so they are MPLS capable. Of these, only .4 has an entry in the LC-ATM (or LC-FR) table, so only it can do LC-ATM (or LC-FR) operation. A row exists only if matching rows exist in ifTable and mplsInterfaceConfTable, and must be deleted shortly after they are.
sections.eli5: Think of a class list, then a shorter list of kids who play soccer, then a still shorter list of goalies. Each shorter list only has names from the longer one.

sections.title: The LC-ATM and LC-FR Objects
sections.content:
The mplsLcAtmStdInterfaceConfTable has objects for the control VPI and VCI, the unlabeled-traffic VPI and VCI, whether the interface can do ATM VC merge (mplsLcAtmStdVcMerge, default false), whether it is directly connected (mplsLcAtmVcDirectlyConnected, default true), a VPI for indirectly connected interfaces (mplsLcAtmLcAtmVPI, default 0), plus RowStatus and StorageType. For indirectly connected interfaces, the label is encoded entirely in the VCI field.

The authors limit control and unlabeled VPI and VCI to single values, which is more restrictive than RFC 3035 allows but reflects widespread implementation. The control and unlabeled VCI MUST not be equal, and the control and unlabeled VPI should not be equal.

The mplsLcFrStdInterfaceConfTable has minimum and maximum DLCI values for traffic and for control, plus RowStatus and StorageType. This MIB does not support mixed labeled and unlabeled traffic, although RFC 3034 allows it, because that capability does not seem to be used operationally. The traffic and control DLCI ranges MUST not overlap.
sections.eli5: Each special link has a few settings, like which lane is for control messages and which lanes are for regular traffic. The lanes for different jobs must not be the same.

sections.title: Row Management and Compliance
sections.content:
A manager creates or deletes rows with the RowStatus object. The matching ifEntry and mplsInterfaceConfEntry MUST exist first. If a manager tries to create a row for an interface that does not support LC-ATM (or LC-FR), the agent MUST return an inconsistentValue error. In a writable table, objects cannot be modified once the row is active(1), except the row status and storage type.

Each module defines a full compliance statement, where devices can be monitored and configured, and a read-only compliance statement, where objects only need read access. Each has one mandatory object group, mplsLcAtmStdIfGroup or mplsLcFrStdIfGroup.
sections.eli5: You can only add a name to the special list if the person is already on the main list. After a name is made official, you cannot change its details.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC warns that anything that can be configured can be incorrectly configured, with potentially disastrous results. The read-write and read-create objects in both interface configuration tables can provision LC-enabled interfaces, and unauthorized access could disrupt traffic, especially if traffic is already established.

Read access may also be sensitive, since the tables reveal the interfaces, their configuration and links to other MPLS data. SNMPv3 VACM and USM MUST be used with any v3 agent that implements these modules. It is RECOMMENDED to use the SNMPv3 security features, including cryptographic authentication and privacy, and deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: The settings panel can break the network if the wrong person touches it. So only trusted people should get the key, and even looking should be limited.

sections.title: IANA Assignments
sections.content: MPLS standards-track MIB modules are rooted under the mplsStdMIB subtree, as requested in the MPLS-TC-STD-MIB (RFC 3811). IANA assigned { mplsStdMIB 9 } to MPLS-LC-ATM-STD-MIB and { mplsStdMIB 10 } to MPLS-LC-FR-STD-MIB. New assignments there can only be made through a Standards Action.
sections.eli5: Each new list gets its own official number so nobody mixes them up. These two got numbers 9 and 10.

viz.caption: OBJECTS IN EACH MODULE (RFC 4368, SECTIONS 7 AND 8)

items.title: LC-ATM
items.text: Control VPI/VCI, unlabeled VPI/VCI, VC merge, direct connection, indirect VPI.

items.title: LC-FR
items.text: Min and max DLCI for traffic, and min and max DLCI for control.

items.title: Both
items.text: RowStatus to create or delete rows, and StorageType.
